name: Magnetic Torsion Blade MTB-7 'Shearwater'
description:
The MTB-7 is a single-edged combat blade, 28 centimeters in length, constructed from a segmented ferromagnetic alloy with a hollow spine housing a miniaturized linear magnetic acceleration coil array. When activated, the coil array generates a rotating magnetic field along the blade's long axis, causing the blade's segmented construction to torque microscopically — approximately 0.4 degrees of torsional flex per segment. The cumulative effect along the blade's length is a continuous corkscrew motion at the cutting edge, invisible to the naked eye but mechanically equivalent to a high-speed drill bit at the point of tissue contact.

The torsional motion transforms the MTB-7's wound profile entirely. A standard thrust with a conventional blade creates a linear puncture channel. The same thrust with the MTB-7 active creates a helical wound cavity that expands as the blade penetrates, shredding tissue in a widening spiral pattern. Extraction is equally destructive — pulling the blade free while active widens the wound channel significantly, a feature that operators describe clinically as 'maximizing effect on withdrawal.' Against augmentation casings, the torsional cutting edge can bore through Grade 1-2 subdermal plating that would deflect a conventional blade entirely.

TESSERA CORPONATION produced the MTB-7 under a defense contract that was subsequently classified, which has led to considerable speculation about which branch of the GLMZ municipal authority originally commissioned it. The weapon entered black market circulation approximately 18 months after its presumed initial deployment, suggesting either a supply chain compromise or a deliberate off-the-books distribution strategy by parties within TESSERA. The blade's segmented construction means it can be disassembled into components that individually register as non-weapons on standard scanners, a feature that almost certainly was not accidental.
specifications:
blade length: 28 cm
total weight: 0.9 kg
blade material: Segmented ferromagnetic alloy (classified composition)
torsion rate: 0.4 degrees per segment per activation cycle
segments: 14 active segments
activation time: 0.2 seconds to full torsion from cold start
power source: Grip-integrated micro-battery, 90 minutes continuous operation
wound profile: Helical cavity, 1.8x standard puncture volume at full depth
scanner profile: Individual components below weapons detection threshold on standard municipal scanners
augmentation penetration: Effective against Grade 1-2 subdermal plating
tactical_use: The MTB-7 is used almost exclusively in assassination and close-quarters elimination scenarios. The standard technique is deactivated carry with activation occurring at the moment of initial penetration, ensuring the torsion effect is active throughout the full strike depth rather than lost on surface contact. Skilled operators activate on withdrawal rather than on entry when attempting to minimize initial resistance — entering as a conventional blade and activating during extraction to maximize the exit wound. The disassembly capability is used for checkpoint infiltration, with operators reassembling under 40 seconds from component carry.
cultural_context: The MTB-7 occupies a specific niche in GLMZ's assassination culture — it is a weapon that signals professional intent and significant resources. Street violence does not require a magnetic torsion blade; its presence at a crime scene is read by investigators and underworld figures alike as a marker of contract killing or institutional violence. The classified origins and TESSERA CORPONATION's official silence on the weapon's existence have made it into something of a collector's item among weapons enthusiasts, with functional units commanding extraordinary black market prices. There are persistent rumors of a civilian 'sport' variant with reduced torsion yield, but no confirmed examples exist.
known_users: Contract assassins operating at the corporate level
TESSERA CORPONATION covert operations personnel (officially nonexistent)
A small number of elite mercenary operatives with the contacts to source one
Municipal investigators who have logged it as evidence and not returned it
story_hooks: A MTB-7 is found at a murder scene, but the wound profile is wrong — the torsion pattern indicates the blade was rotating in the opposite direction from standard factory configuration, suggesting either a modified unit or a second manufacturer producing counterfeits with reversed coil winding.

TESSERA CORPONATION quietly hires the players to recover all black-market MTB-7 units in circulation before a municipal weapons audit that would expose the classified contract's existence — the number of units they're asked to find is significantly higher than the number that should exist if the original contract is accurate.

A player character is given a disassembled MTB-7 as payment for a job, only to discover that one of the segments contains a micro-transmitter broadcasting their location — whoever gave them the weapon wants to know exactly where they go with it.
